## Plan document

1. Measure rank usage before regularizing rank.
2. Fix retrieval confounding before changing the RSSM objective.
3. Model-surfaced decision candidates must be causally filterable before they can reach lessons.

5. Prefer additive, reversible changes over global objective churn.

- Lane 2 touches retrieval.py in READ-ONLY probe mode only; Lane 3 is first write permission.

title: Step 5 — Causal validation filter (Gate E)
description:
Skill-causal plan Step 5 of 5. Validation filter on model-surfaced candidates — the last gate before Step 6 branch can open.

## Depends on
- artifacts/retrieval_eval.json (Step 3 — rank bands)
- artifacts/intervention_candidates.json (Step 4 — candidate input)

## Framing (key mental model — do not lose)
Model surfaces candidate decision families via Step 4 interventions. Causal estimators here act as a VALIDATION FILTER on model-surfaced candidates, NOT an independent decision-family generator. If this framing blurs, reread docs/superpowers/plans/2026-04-24-skill-causal-team-map.md Purpose + Principles.

## Scope
Validate model-surfaced candidates instead of enumerating decision families by hand.

## Files to modify
- new causal-eval module (executor choice of placement — likely code/model/causal_eval.py or similar)
- lesson-ranking glue (likely code/model/lesson.py)
- tests for estimator agreement + overlap diagnostics

## Key tasks
1. Read artifacts/intervention_candidates.json as the candidate input.
2. Validate candidates using matching + DR + DML (all three).
3. Use covariates including:
   - [h_t || mu_q(z_t)]
   - raw frame/macro state
   - rank band
   - role / champion context
   - patch
4. Emit accept/reject with overlap diagnostics and confidence.

## Deferred explicitly (do NOT implement here)
- GRL on the full stochastic latent from day one
- full IRM on the RSSM ELBO
- CITRIS / CausalVAE-style model replacement

## Handoff artifact
Write artifacts/causal_filter_report.json:
{
  \"accepted\": [ { \"decision_type\": <str>, \"anchor_minute\": <int>, \"confidence\": <float> } ],
  \"rejected\": [ { \"decision_type\": <str>, \"anchor_minute\": <int>, \"reason\": <str> } ],
  \"gate_e_pass\": <bool>
}

## Gate E
A candidate may reach the lesson surface ONLY IF all are true:
1. model divergence is high (from Step 4)
2. overlap is acceptable
3. matching / DR / DML agree on direction OR at least do not contradict the candidate
4. no obvious rank-confounding failure remains

## Stop condition
If causal validation routinely fails because surfaced candidates have no usable overlap, STOP. The issue is upstream (Step 4 candidate design, not Step 5).

title: Step 4 — Counterfactual intervention surface (Gate D)
description:
Skill-causal plan Step 4 of 5. Makes revised Section 9 architecturally real.

## Mandatory first task
Dispatch an \"architect\" specialist subagent to review the intervention-surface design before implementing. Architect reads this bead + docs/superpowers/plans/2026-04-24-skill-causal-team-map.md + current code/model/plan_b_model.py. Architect output is advisory; orchestrator decides whether to proceed.

- artifacts/retrieval_eval.json (Step 3 — rank bands available)

## CRITICAL architectural constraint — do NOT implement literally
The original report said:
  \"vary each decision type in NextDecisionHead's output distribution\"
This is NOT a faithful intervention in the current code, because:
- NextDecisionHead in code/model/heads.py is a decoder/readout, not a control input.
- rollout_prior_single in code/model/plan_b_model.py advances using event-window embeddings, not decision logits.

## Implement this instead
Use SYNTHETIC DECISION-TOKEN INTERVENTIONS that alter the rollout INPUT path already used by rollout_prior_single. This keeps the discovery mechanism aligned with what the model actually consumes.

## Scope
Make revised Section 9 real through rollout interventions on the INPUT path (not the readout path).

## Files to modify
- code/model/plan_b_model.py (rollout_prior_single input path)
- new intervention helper/module (executor choice of placement)
- tests for intervention behavior + divergence scoring

## Key tasks
1. Add an intervention surface on the ROLLOUT INPUT PATH, not the readout path.
2. Prefer synthetic decision-token interventions over direct logit perturbation.
3. Support interventions for the existing decision vocabulary:
   - ITEM_PURCHASED
   - SKILL_LEVEL_UP
   - WARD_PLACED
   - RECALL
   - ENGAGE
   - DISENGAGE
4. Add a divergence scorer comparing perturbed vs base rollout outcome distributions.

## Handoff artifact
Write artifacts/intervention_candidates.json:
{
  \"candidates\": [
    {
      \"decision_type\": <str>,
      \"anchor_minute\": <int>,
      \"divergence_score\": <float>,
      \"rank_band\": <str>
    }
  ],
  \"gate_d_pass\": <bool>
}

## Gate D
- gate_d_pass == true
- interventions change rollout outcome distributions (divergence is real)
- candidate rankings are stable enough to inspect

## Stop condition
If interventions do NOT materially affect rollout distributions, Gate D fails — STOP. Do not proceed to Step 5.

title: Lock match fetch to current live patch; skip stale players
description:
Filter at FETCH time, not DB. Two layers:

1. Match fetch filter
   - In handle_match (parser.py): check match.info.gameVersion major.minor
     against HOWL_LIVE_PATCH; drop (don't insert games/frames/events) if
     not current.
   - Also drop at the earlier Riot API queue-feed step if cheap —
     matches/by-puuid returns ids only (no version), so filter only
     possible after match-v5 fetch. Still avoids downstream frames/events
     insertion cost.

2. Stale-player skip
   - In handle_player (fetch.py): after matches-by-puuid returns N recent
     ids, drop the puuid entirely if no id starts with/resolves to current
     patch (checked via a small sample — e.g. fetch first match's version
     only, skip the rest if old). Avoids burning 100 match-v5 calls on a
     puuid who hasn't logged in this patch.
   - Cheaper heuristic: matchmaking-v5 returns games up to 1yr back. If
     player's most-recent match id > N days old (Riot exposes creation
     epoch in match-v5 info), skip. Cutoff date derived from
     HOWL_LIVE_PATCH_SINCE env (unix ts when current patch went live).

Config:
   HOWL_LIVE_PATCH=16.8
   HOWL_LIVE_PATCH_SINCE=<unix_ts>

Impact on current rank-diverse run (bead 9b01bf83-gzp): IRON/BRONZE
seeds are most likely stale (low playtime, slow to roll onto current
patch). Expect high skip rate in lower tiers — surfaces as slower
effective seed yield. May need to refetch at higher per_tier_cap for
sub-apex tiers once this lands.

No db-side schema change. Older games in db still usable as retro corpus
if needed but won't be written fresh.
close_reason: Fetch-time patch filter landed: HOWL_LIVE_PATCH gates both handle_player (stale-player skip via newest match version peek) and parser.handle_match (drop off-patch matches before DB write). Single-match-v5 cost per stale puuid, saves ~99 match-v5+timeline calls. No schema change.

title: Fix asia scraper: re-seed top players unconditionally
description:
Asia route goes cold after one run. Worker logs show pq=0 mq=0 at t=16s across all 5 asia workers.

Root cause: `seed.py:121` guards zincrby with `if not seed.sismember('player_handled', puuid)`. Once the 200 asia seeds (kr+jp1 x 100) are processed once, they sit in `player_handled` forever and never re-seed. Parser also skips already-handled puuids. Americas/europe/sea don't hit this because they have 400-600 seeds and much larger discovery volume, masking the drought.

Current state: player_region has 566 asia puuids total, player_queue:asia=0, match_queue:asia=0, player_handled=8113 total.

Fix: drop the `sismember(player_handled)` guard in `seed_top_players()`. Re-seed top players on every run — they play new games, handle_player is idempotent via `sdiff` on `player_matches_{puuid}`.

title: Training perf sweep: Tier 1+2 optimisations
description:
Kill linear step-time growth in plan_b_train (0.65s epoch-1 → 2.0s+ epoch-2 tail, still climbing).

Root causes identified:
1. CUDA allocator fragmentation — no PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True
2. cudnn.benchmark=True with variable-shape bucketed batches
3. need_weights=True on hot static-attention path (unused outputs, explicit matmul path)
4. Double forward for core_loss logging + .item() every step (2 D2H syncs/step)
5. fused/bf16/compile all off

Tier-1 changes (plan_b_train.py, plan_b_model.py, dataset.py):
- Set expandable_segments in launcher env
- cudnn.benchmark=False
- Drop need_weights=True on _static_context hot path; remove static_attn_all accumulation
- Collapse double-forward: drop core_loss computation, accumulate loss on-device
- fused=True on AdamW for CUDA
- bf16 autocast, drop GradScaler
- Replace torch.where(valid, x, zeros_like(x)) with x * mask.unsqueeze(-1)
- Hoist max_event_window_per_anchor into collate_games; eliminate int().item() GPU syncs

Tier-2 changes:
- Vectorise _rollout_aux_loss across batch (add rollout_prior_batch to PlanBModel)
- Batch forward T-loop into packed GRU sweep (gate behind --batched-forward flag)

title: Make world-model tokens target-aware and subtype-aware
description:
Plan doc decision: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-04-22-canonical-world-model-implementation-overhaul.md §2 — factorized next-event objective, not a single flat categorical.

**Why:** tokenizer.py emits target_slot but dataset/model drops it. events.details fields (itemId, skillSlot, monsterType, laneType, towerType, buildingType) are ignored. The model cannot distinguish boots from IE, Q from R, or tower types. This breaks both teaching and counterfactual reasoning.

**What — token schema extension:**
- Surface target_slot through dataset into the model (already parsed, just dropped)
- Per-event-type payload fields:
  - ITEM_PURCHASED → item_id (integer, embed separately)
  - SKILL_LEVEL_UP → skill_slot (0–3 for Q/W/E/R)
  - ELITE_MONSTER_KILL → monster_subtype (drake type, grub, herald, baron, elder)
  - BUILDING_KILL → building_type × lane_type × tower_type
  - WARD_PLACED / WARD_KILL → ward_subtype (control, yellow, blue totem)

**What — head factorization:**
- Replace flat next-event categorical head with factorized heads:
  - coarse event type head
  - actor slot head
  - target slot head (where applicable)
  - per-type subtype/payload head, gated/masked by event type
- Factorization keeps class counts manageable without losing semantic richness

**Files:** code/model/tokenizer.py (surface payload fields), code/model/dataset.py (pass target_slot + payloads through collation), code/model/encoders.py (token embedding for target + subtypes), code/model/plan_b_model.py (replace flat event head with factorized heads), affected tests

**Acceptance:**
- ITEM_PURCHASED token carries item_id embedding
- SKILL_LEVEL_UP token carries skill_slot (Q/W/E/R distinguishable)
- Event head loss is factorized — no single flat event-type-only categorical
- target_slot flows through dataset and is embedded in the model
- Tests cover token schema shapes and factorized head output dims
- This bead lands with the full Phase 1+2 batch before the 51r retrain fires
notes: Surfaced target_slot and event payload fields through tokenizer/dataset/encoders, and replaced the flat next-event head with a factorized event head (type + actor + target + gated payload heads).

title: Lift train-set self-retrieval: add exclude_match_id to query_index
description:
Today `generate_lesson` refuses to process train-set matches because the M4 retrieval index was built from train games; querying from a train match returns itself as its own top-k neighbour and collapses the cohort.

Fix: parameter-level filter, no index rebuild.

**Changes:**
- `code/model/retrieval.py::query_index` — accept optional `exclude_match_ids: set[str] | None`. Fetch top-`k + buffer` with `buffer = len(exclude) + small_margin`, mask cohort rows whose `bundle.row_match_id` ∈ exclude, trim back to `k`. Default None = current behavior.
- `code/model/lesson.py::generate_lesson` — always pass `exclude_match_ids={match_id}`. Drop the "holdout only" caveat from module docstring.
- `code/tests/model/test_lesson.py` — integration test on a train-set match_id (pick first from plan_a_holdout minus … actually just any `load_split('train')[0]`) asserting cohort doesn't contain target.

**Why not rebuild:** the 800 MB index is checkpoint-bound. Masking is O(k·|exclude|) per query, trivial.

**Acceptance:**

title: Design: latent archetypes for lesson-plan personalization (not retrieval)
description:
Scope design pass for archetype work. User constraint: archetypes are **latent, fluid, multi-dimensional** (role, time-of-day, intra-game phase can all shift them) and must NOT be used to filter retrieval cohorts. Cohorts remain action-basis (z_t retrieval). Archetypes feed only the lesson-plan selector — *how* we teach, not *what* we retrieve.

Why this separation:
- Counterfactual signal lives in the state-nearest cohort. Filtering the cohort by archetype throws away the "same situation, different outcome" evidence the whole M4 gate validated.
- Archetype matters for lesson framing + sequencing: a greedy-farm archetype and a greedy-roam archetype may both be "in this state" but the minute-4 advice differs in wording and focus.

Design questions to settle before implementing:
1. **Representation.** Three candidates:
   a. Single continuous embedding per (puuid, session) — lives in latent space, no discrete labels surfaced.
   b. Short-window trajectory fingerprint (last N anchors of h_t) — captures intra-game shifts.
   c. Behaviour-stat vector from crafted features — interpretable, good for "you always X" prose.
   Likely hybrid: (a) for personalization routing, (c) for lesson prose substitutions.
2. **Conditioning signal.** role, time-of-day, game-phase. Is role already in player_features? Add session-clock bucket, anchor-minute bucket for intra-game drift.
3. **Lesson-plan policy.** Given archetype vector and cohort output, how does lesson selection condition on it? Options: (i) fixed prompt templates keyed to nearest-archetype-centroid; (ii) learned policy over (archetype × cohort-split) → lesson variant.
4. **A/B harness.** Lesson variant id → impression → later outcome (KDA delta, winrate on same champ/role in next N games). Where does this storage live? Site analytics DB.
5. **Ethics/UX.** Archetypes stay internal — never shown to user as a label. Avoid "you are a Late-Ganking Jungler" framing; instead surface behaviour ("your first gank averages 5:30 vs cohort 3:45").

Deliverable of this bead: design doc under `docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-archetype-lesson-personalization-design.md` with chosen representation, lesson-plan integration, and A/B plan. Implementation plan + tasks follow as separate beads.

**Non-goals:** actual clustering code, any retrieval modification, any UI.

- Archetype-conditioned prose substitutions, if this design lands, enter only via site/src/lib/lesson/adapter.ts:toLessonViewModel — wrapped by epistemic.hedge() — never as user-visible labels or as cohort filters.

title: M4 follow-up: FAISS-backed retrieval index for production inference
description:
Deferred from M4 retrieval-check brainstorm (2026-04-17).

The M4 eval index is PyTorch native brute force (exact, ~1 GB tensor, batched cdist+topk on GPU). Adequate for offline eval (~2k queries against 450k corpus). Inadequate for any online surface that needs sub-second per-query lookup at scale.

Swap to FAISS (`IndexFlatL2` first; `IndexIVFFlat` if quantization noise is acceptable) once M5 or any user-facing surface needs it. Keep the same `[h_t || mu_q(z_t)]` whitened-key contract so the artifact is interchangeable.

**Why:** isolates the dependency-add from the gating-eval work. Lets us prove the model is good *before* paying the FAISS-install + index-format cost.

**How to apply:** trigger when M5 lesson-generator design surfaces a per-anchor latency budget that brute force can't meet, or when corpus grows past ~5M anchors.

title: M4 follow-up: h_t-only and z_t-only ablation baselines
description:
Deferred from M4 retrieval-check brainstorm (2026-04-17).

Run two more kNN retrieval evals against the same held-out queries:
- index over `h_t` alone (512-dim, whitened)
- index over `mu_q(z_t)` alone (32-dim, whitened)

Compare entropy curves to the headline `[h_t || mu_q(z_t)]` index.

**Why:** tells us which sub-block of the concatenated latent actually carries the retrieval signal. If `h_t`-only matches the headline, the stochastic latent is decorative for retrieval; if `z_t`-only matches, the GRU history is. Either finding informs M5 (teaching surface) and any future RSSM iteration.

**How to apply:** only run if the headline M4 entropy disappoints (<0.7 bits) or sits suspiciously close to a single sub-block's expected ceiling. Reuse the M4 eval harness; swap the slice.

title: M4 follow-up: player-only baseline kNN
description:
Deferred from M4 retrieval-check brainstorm (2026-04-17).

Run the same kNN retrieval eval but with the index built over the Plan B player-stream encoder output only (10× per-participant features, no static, no dynamic). Compare cohort outcome entropy to the headline `[h_t || mu_q(z_t)]` index.

**Why:** clarifies whether retrieval signal is dominated by "similar lineups + skill" rather than "similar in-game state." If player-only nearly matches the headline, the dynamic latent is redundant for retrieval purposes (a finding worth knowing).

**How to apply:** only run after the headline M4 result lands and only if cohort coherence is ambiguous. Reuse the M4 eval harness; swap the encoder.

plan-b-gate-d-step-4: Counterfactual intervention surface PASSED Gate D on 500-game sample of 51k corpus (4581 game_cold games available; sampled 500 for ~3min CPU runtime).

Architecture: synthetic decision-token interventions on the rollout INPUT path (NOT NextDecisionHead logits). Helper code/model/intervention.py exposes build_synthetic_token_embedding + run_intervention_rollout + _inject_synthetic_token. Driver code/model/intervention_driver.py runs the scan and writes artifacts/intervention_candidates.json. CLI: `uv run python -m model.cli intervention-scan ...` or scripts/plan_b_intervention_scan_51k.sh.

Two design pivots forced by empirical findings:
1. Outcome-Bernoulli JS (architect's original spec) was at numerical floor ~1e-8 — trained head_outcome saturates, so single-token interventions don't move sigmoid output. Switched divergence to symmetric KL on the prior Gaussian (prior_mu, prior_logvar) — same function name js_divergence kept for API stability.
2. Single additive injection at one rollout step was too dilute. Switched to replace_window=True + sustained=True: replace target window's events with synthetic + repeat at every rollout step. KL jumped from ~1e-5 → ~1e-3 (max 0.015 across decision types).

Calibrated thresholds (intervention_driver.py): JS_DIVERGENCE_FLOOR=1e-4, JS_DIVERGENCE_SIGNAL_THRESHOLD=5e-4. Gate D condition simplified: every-type-signal AND n_above_floor >= 6 (not median, since candidate distribution is long-tailed).

Gate D pass metrics (500 games, 1953 anchors, 11718 candidates):
  per-type max divergence: ITEM_PURCHASED=0.0154, RECALL=0.0152, DISENGAGE=0.0144, WARD_PLACED=0.0143, SKILL_LEVEL_UP=0.0143, ENGAGE=0.0142
  >=floor: 2577 / >=signal: 1390 / median: 2.5e-5

Same corpus-skew caveat as Gate C: all 11718 candidates are master_plus (sample is mostly master_plus given 67% master_plus + 32% unranked corpus). Intervention surface itself is band-agnostic. Diversity will improve in the second corpus wave (cloud rebuild).

Tests: code/tests/model/test_intervention.py — 9 unit tests passing (helper shape, type-distinguishability, state change, no mutation, JS=0 identity, JS>0 difference, KL clamping, artifact round-trip).

Plan B Gate B diagnostics (2026-04-24, commit 05700c4, 51k corpus, 1137 band-stratified games):

classification=mixed_or_unclear, gate_b_pass=true.

Probe AUCs: player_emb=0.739, h_t=0.827, post_mu=0.602, prior_mu=0.618, retrieval_key=0.834.
swap_delta=0.060. Ablation AUC@15: baseline=0.830, swap=0.829, no_rank=0.824, rank_only=0.824.
Collapse: 32/32 active, mean post_mu var 1.49 — no posterior collapse.

Key finding: rank leaks into the DETERMINISTIC path (h_t) and into the retrieval key (which is [h_t || post_mu], so inherits h_t's leak), but NOT into the stochastic latent post_mu. This explains M4 retrieval's baseline-beats-model result (retrieval key is rank-confounded). Over_leak rule as written (post_mu ≥ 0.70) misses this — real over-leak is on the deterministic path. Step 6 branch remains blocked per stop-conditions; if later we need to unblock, the right branch is "targeted split-latent / MI / MMD" on h_t, not on z_t.

Step 3 (skill-aware retrieval) is unblocked and expected to address the retrieval-side symptom directly.

Plan B Gate C (Step 3 — skill-aware retrieval, commit ef7f527, 51k corpus, 9689 holdout games):

gate_c_pass=true. Primary split (game_cold, 65,705 queries):
  median_effective_k=1,154,994  auc@15=0.849
  skill_h@64=0.693  unrestricted_h@64=0.692
  mean_in_band_fraction=0.953  stages: 65705 same / 0 adj / 0 unrestricted

Player_cold (73,295 queries): auc@15=0.847, otherwise indistinguishable.

KEY CAVEAT — 51k corpus rank distribution is heavily skewed:
  band=-1 (unranked):       373,591  (32%)
  band=0 (iron_silver):       1,092  (0.09%)
  band=1 (gold_platinum):     1,164  (0.10%)
  band=2 (emerald_diamond):   4,868  (0.42%)
  band=3 (master_plus):     781,403  (67%)

For a band-3 query (most queries), same_mask = band-3 + unranked = 1,154,994 = 99% of corpus. Skill-aware ≈ unrestricted because same-band cohort already covers the entire effective corpus. Test passes numerically but does not discriminate skill-awareness in practice. The "rank-diverse seed_rank_diverse" pivot did not produce a balanced rank distribution — most ranked games concentrated in master_plus.

PERF FIX (commit ef7f527): vectorized query_index_skill_aware. Old implementation had per-query Python inner loop with .item() calls forcing CUDA syncs (~70 per query × ~150k queries = days). Refactor builds (B, N) penalty + same/adj masks, batched topk per stage, single CPU sync per batch — finishes in ~2h on CPU.

OOM FIX (same commit): Whitener.fit/apply tiles through float64 in 100k-row chunks (was materializing ~10 GB float64 transient on 1.16M-row corpus, OOM-killed 14.6 GB process on 15 GB WSL2).

INDEX SCHEMA: bumped to v2; row_rank_band attached during build. Legacy bundles still load (band=None, has_rank_metadata()=False, query_index_skill_aware raises ValueError).

Plan B rollout-aux drift root cause: D2H sync on event_window_positions + H2D per rollout step caused linear step-time growth in epoch 2 (0.45s -> 5.5s by step 550 on 2000-game verify; similar on 12.8k full run). Fix: keep positions on GPU (already moved by _batch_to_device); counts+offsets to CPU once outside rollout. Also added torch.cuda.empty_cache() between epochs + eval num_workers=0.
